lesson.title: 911 – Procedure 104: Vehicle Checks & Automatic Routing Codes
objectives: Use vehicle check codes 10-14 through 10-19 correctly.
Apply the language restrictions for 'stolen' and 'hit/no hit' wording.
Explain the purpose of automatic routing codes such as 10-60, I8, H, and H8.
Select appropriate codes for pursuits and disabled vehicle incidents.

questions.stem: A unit asks you to run a plate, and the system shows the vehicle IS reported stolen. According to Procedure 104, how should you transmit this result?

choices.text: Say, “Vehicle is stolen,” in plain language.
Transmit code 10-16 and do NOT use the word “stolen.”

questions.solution: 10-16 is VEHICLE IS REPORTED STOLEN and Procedure 104 specifically states DO NOT transmit the word STOLEN over the air; use the code instead.

questions.stem: Which code is used when an RMP advises the dispatcher that they are in a chase or pursuit of a vehicle?
questions.solution: Procedure 104 lists 10-60 as I BROADCAST (CHASE/PURSUIT) when an RMP advises they are in a chase/pursuit of a vehicle.

questions.stem: For codes 10-14, 10-15, 10-16, and 10-17, the word “stolen” should NEVER be transmitted over the air. The code itself carries that meaning.
When a warrant check is positive, it is acceptable to say 'HIT' over the air as long as you also give code 10-18.
For code 10-18 WARRANT CHECK SHOWS ACTIVE WARRANT, Procedure 104 instructs dispatchers: DO NOT transmit the word __________ over the air.
For code 10-19 WARRANT CHECK NEGATIVE, dispatchers are told not to transmit the words “__________” over the air.
Match each vehicle check code from Procedure 104 with the correct meaning.
answer: OCCUPIED AND SUSPICIOUS VERIFY IF STOLEN (word 'stolen' not transmitted).
VERIFY IF STOLEN OCCUPIED OR NOT (ascertain unit’s location upon request).
VEHICLE IS REPORTED STOLEN (do NOT transmit the word 'stolen'; use the code).
VEHICLE IS NOT REPORTED STOLEN (do NOT transmit the word 'stolen'; use the code).

questions.stem: Match each automatic routing/research code with its description.
answer: I BROADCAST (CHASE/PURSUIT) – RMP advises they are in chase/pursuit of a vehicle.
BROADCAST/LMT AC HWY – broadcast and limited access highway routing.
RESEARCH (DISABLED VEHICLE) – unit advises they are pushing a disabled vehicle creating a hazard.
RESEARCH/LMT AC HWY – disabled vehicle on a limited access highway.
